I can't reproduce this on 4.5.beta1 on my end (I get 5600 FPS in both cases), but I have a much faster CPU/GPU:

<details open>

<summary>PC specifications</summary>

- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090
- **RAM:** 64 GB (2×32 GB DDR5-6000 CL30)
- **SSD:** Solidigm P44 Pro 2 TB
- **OS:** Linux (Fedora 42)
</details>

However, if I force software rendering through Xephyr + llvmpipe, I will get much lower FPS in both cases. In this situation, scaling has a significant cost (Xephyr is at `1280×960` in both cases, but it displays lower-resolution apps centered):

- 320x240: 620 FPS (1.61 mspf)
- 1280x960: 385 FPS (2.60 mspf)

This is a frametime difference of around 1 millisecond per frame. Given this is software rendering we're talking about (which scales *very* poorly with resolution), I consider this to be within acceptable limits.

When doing performance comparisons, remember to compare frametimes (milliseconds per frame/mspf) instead of frames per second, as FPS is a non-linear measurement.

Here, the difference in frametime between the two tests is 2.83 mspf (`1000/354.0 - 1000/1843.0`). This looks significant, but for not-so-recent integrated graphics (especially on battery or a low power profile), it's not out of the ordinary. Remember the blitting the viewport to a higher resolution window *does* have a performance cost in any engine (even software rendering is impacted by this).

> so wait, this means my laptop is using software rendering instead of its igpu?

Probably not, but you can check by opening Godot from a terminal and looking at the `OpenGL Renderer` line on startup. If it says `llvmpipe`, then it's using software rendering. On Direct3D 12, the equivalent software renderer is `WARP`.

Tested in both `v4.6.dev4` and `v4.5.1.stable`. My setup is also quite modern and I hit ~2500FPS on an AMD RX 6750 XT, so the difference in FPS between scaling the window is very little, around ~50FPS. It's worth pointing out that when attempting to identify performance issues on graphics, it's really important to use a moderately complex scene for more consistent results. This MRP is too simple, so it's hard to gauge whether there is indeed a significant impact on the viewport blitting, as @Calinou mentions. I've modified the MRP to instance 10k of the example mesh, which does lower my FPS to a more sensible ~30FPS: In this case, changing the window resolution has basically no impact in FPS. Please test if in your setup this is also the same (do adjust the number of spawned objects in `main_scene.gd` to get a similar FPS value according to your setup) [mrp_updated.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23834215/mrp_updated.zip)
